Shaxi Old Town: Tea Horse Trail Heritage
After breakfast, your guide and driver will meet you at your hotel to explore Shaxi Old Town, an important historical stop on the ancient Tea Horse Trail. Walk the narrow, cobblestone alleyways where Yi and Bai ethnic minorities continue to maintain their traditions alongside residents who have preserved the town's character for centuries. Observe intricately carved wooden entrances and glimpse the well-fenced, attractive courtyards hidden behind many of the homes. Siding Square forms the center of the old town, established as a Tea Horse route hub during the Tang dynasty in 618. UNESCO recognizes Shaxi as one of the most intact tea-trading towns remaining in China—a place where history remains tangible in every corner. Return to your hotel in Shaxi for the evening.

The Qinghai-Tibet Railway to Lhasa
Depart Xi'an on the Qinghai-Tibet Railway, one of China's greatest engineering achievements and the world's highest railway line. The route travels northeast from Xi'an to Xining (approximately 12 hours), then west to Golmud, before turning south toward Lhasa. day_text:
Trek to Everest Base Camp and Return to Pheriche
A very early start sets the tone for this demanding day. The trek crosses the Khumbu Glacier for several hours along a trail weaving past translucent ice pinnacles and crevasses. At Everest Base Camp (5,364 meters), you'll stand at the staging point for Everest ascents, with views up into the Khumbu Icefall where climbing activity is often visible. If an expedition is in residence, the sense of scale becomes immediate.

The return route gains elevation to provide a spectacular perspective of the Khumbu Icefall and the route to the South Col—views worth the extra effort. From there, the descent is mostly downhill: past Gorak Shep, Lobuche, Duglha, and finally to Pheriche at 4,320 meters. The Himalayan Rescue Association maintains a trekkers' aid post here, worth a visit to understand the medical support systems that serve the region's high-altitude trekking community.

atom: Ura village — watch masked dances performing the thunderbolt step
day_text:
Ura Festival: Masked Dances, Spiritual Ceremonies & Purification Rites
Drive to Ura village for the festival. Locals walk from surrounding valleys dressed in their finest clothes to attend the three-day celebrations. Masked dances dominate: dancers perform the thunderbolt step, their robes of coloured brocade spinning as they move. The masks themselves — glorious demonic and animal forms — invoke festival deities and enact purification rites. Watch for the Atsara, the festival clown, who mimics dancers and entertains spectators. The dances function as spiritual theatre, telling stories where good triumphs over evil and depicting historical events, particularly those surrounding Padmasambhava (Guru Rinpoche), Bhutan's patron saint. Underlying purpose is spiritual; luck is increased and misfortune dissipated through the ceremony.

Khuvsgul Lake Arrival
Travel northward to Khuvsgul Lake on a full day of driving (approximately 400km from Sod Camp). Stop for lunch near Moron, capital of Khuvsgul province, then continue to camp on the lake's shore. Khuvsgul is Asia's second-largest freshwater lake, covering 2,760 square kilometers and formed approximately 2 million years ago. It sits on the boundary between Central Asian steppes and Siberian taiga forest and is home to the Tsaatan people, also known as Dukha, who sustain themselves primarily through reindeer herding. Overnight at a standard ger camp (upgrade available).

Angkor's Small Circuit by Bicycle
A 40-kilometre cycle explores Angkor's Small Circuit. The route includes Takeo (a pyramid temple), Ta Prohm (jungle-clad and famous from film), and Sras Srang, known as the King's bathing pond. The main focus is Angkor Thom, the vast walled royal city, where Bayon—a temple famed for its many large carved smiling stone faces—stands at the centre. Other sites within Angkor Thom include Baphuon pyramid, Phimeanakas, and the Terrace of the Elephants and Terrace of the Leper King, both serving historical ceremonial functions. After lunch, Angkor Wat itself is visited. In the late afternoon, cyclists reach an excellent vantage point for a sunset view of the temple complex.

The trail is swept with loose scree; you may encounter a local herding a donkey along the path. The experience—exhausted, resting atop a rock, watching fading sunlight dance between distant peaks and then dance on the river far below—sums up the trek's singular character. This is counted among southwest China's most significant trekking routes. Stay overnight at a guesthouse in the gorge.

day_text:
Korean Demilitarized Zone & K-pop Dance Class
An hour-long bus ride north from Seoul takes you to Imjingak, where breakfast is available before continuing to Dorasan Station, the northernmost train stop in South Korea. Built decades ago with the intention of eventually connecting Seoul and Pyongyang, the station remains a striking reminder of divided history. Walk the platform and pick up a souvenir train ticket (1000 KRW) as a tangible piece of this unique site.

From Dora Observatory, binoculars bring the nearest North Korean villages into focus across the border. The 3rd Tunnel, excavated by North Korean forces during the Cold War, descends approximately 170 meters toward the DMZ—a sobering proximity that brings the division into stark relief. On the return bus to Seoul, there's an opportunity to hear firsthand accounts from a North Korean defector.

Back in the city, an included K-pop dance class introduces you to the choreography of international K-pop songs. The 90-minute session requires no prior dance experience, just willingness to learn from professional instructors.

If dance isn't your preference, alternatives include Myeongdong Cathedral or a quirky cat café. For the evening, consider the Nanta Show, a comedic cooking performance that relies on physical humor rather than language. Or venture into Itaewon's eclectic mix of international restaurants and bars, or head to the upscale clubs and lounges of Gangnam. The choice shapes how your day concludes—whether you're still processing the weight of the DMZ or fully immersed in Seoul's energy.

day_text:
Arrival in Seoul: Cheonggyecheon Stream and Myeongdong Orientation
Arrive in Seoul throughout the day and check into Hotel Prince (or similar). As fellow travellers settle in at their own pace, there are no planned activities until the evening group meeting.

At 6 p.m., meet your CEO and fellow travellers for your Welcome Moment. This is your opportunity to connect with your group and learn what to expect from the tour ahead. Your CEO will brief you on the practicalities of travelling through South Korea—where to find supermarkets, main squares, ATMs, and other essentials—before heading out on an orientation walk.

The walk begins at Cheonggyecheon Stream, an 8.4-kilometre waterway restored as a public space that cuts through the heart of downtown Seoul. The walk covers approximately 2 kilometres and takes 45–60 minutes at a leisurely pace. As you walk, you'll pass small waterfalls and nearly two dozen overhead bridges, gaining a sense of the city's geography and character. This restored stream is both a functional transport corridor and a gathering place for locals, offering a calm counterpoint to Seoul's intensity.

From there, you'll move into Myeongdong, a densely packed commercial district situated roughly 20 minutes' walk from the stream. The neighbourhood is a sensory experience—street food carts line the pavements, major shopping malls tower overhead, and entertainment venues draw crowds constantly. It's a quintessential Seoul experience and a good introduction to the city's commercial heart.

After the orientation walk, you have the option to join your CEO and fellow travellers for a group dinner, or explore on your own. Check the notice board in your hotel lobby (or ask reception) for the official meeting time and place if you'd like to join the group.

Before you venture out, it's worth noting that South Korea's efficient train network will be your main transport method throughout this tour. You'll spend most days on foot and will need to carry your own luggage through busy train stations and crowded streets. Please ensure you are fit enough to manage this level of daily movement and comfortable carrying your belongings for extended periods.

The descent involves crossing a small glacier, then follows pastures with excellent views of Ama Dablam and the north face of Cholatse. Dzongla (4,830m) is reached after 7–8 hours. Overnight in a lodge on full board.

atom: Punakha to Bumthang — drive eastward through high mountain landscapes
day_text:
Trongsa Dzong & Drive to Bumthang
Leave Punakha eastward through some of Bhutan's most layered terrain. Stop at Trongsa Dzong, which commands views from miles away and serves as gateway to central Bhutan. After visiting the fortress, continue through high mountain landscapes to Bumthang, the cultural heartland and home of Ura Festival.

atom: Pidurangala Rock — take in panoramic views
day_text:
Colombo's Colonial and Urban Landscape — Departure
Depending on your flight departure time, explore Colombo's urban mix of Victorian colonial buildings, modern commercial districts, and the Old Parliament Buildings. Visit the Kelaniya Temple, a major Buddhist shrine north of the city center, then proceed to the airport for departure. Alternatively, if your flight departs early morning, transfer directly to the airport for check-in.

atom: Ruluos town — visit the local market
day_text:
Kompong Phluk: Rural Cycling, Floating Villages, and Sunset Hike
You bicycle on small back roads through rural landscapes and villages to the temple of Bakong, then continue to Ruluos town and its local market. Following the Ruluos River, you board small wooden boats to Kompong Phluk, a medieval floating village where houses stand on stilts. After exploring the local wat, you board a larger boat cruising through flooded forest and across the great lake to Chong Kneas, an expansive floating village. You then travel to Phnom Krom for a short hike and a sunset view before returning to Siem Reap. The twenty-kilometer biking distance includes varied terrain, and the evening is at leisure.

atom: Angkor's Small Circuit — cycle Ta Prohm, Bayon, Angkor Thom, and Angkor Wat
day_text:
Stung Treng to Preah Vihear: Rolling Hills and Clifftop Temple
A morning transfer heads north toward Kulen Prum Tep Wildlife Sanctuary before cycling begins. The 70-kilometre route gradually changes from flat terrain to rolling hills as it approaches the Thai border. The destination is Preah Vihear, a Hindu temple complex from the Angkorian period, built atop the Poy Tady Cliff in the Dangrek Mountains at 525 metres elevation. The site is UNESCO-protected and renowned not only for its architecture but for its dramatic clifftop position with panoramic views of the surrounding landscape and into Thailand. A 4-wheel-drive vehicle ascends to the temple top for two hours of exploration. Most visitors are Khmer pilgrims who have travelled considerable distances to view the handiwork of their ancestors. Accommodation: Preah Vihear Jaya Hotel, Deluxe Room.

atom: Iizaka Onsen — ride smooth riverside cycling road into town
day_text:
Miharu to Iizaka: Mountain Views and Hanamiyama
A 70-kilometer ride with 900 meters of elevation gain takes you through peaceful villages, steep climbs, and panoramic views of the Azuma mountain range. Along the way, a sakura tree decorated with a Jizo Buddha statue marks a quiet location. Hanamiyama hill—maintained by local residents and covered in blooming sakura alongside seasonal flowers—offers a short walk to survey the landscape. The day concludes on a smooth riverside cycling road into Iizaka Onsen. An onsen hotel with kaiseki-style dinner provides the evening's rest.

atom: Hong Island — kayak lagoon and cave passages and visit panoramic coastal viewpoint
day_text:
Bangkok Temples, Canals & Markets
Start from your hotel and explore Bangkok's core by water and foot. Visit Wat Arun and Wat Pho, two major temple compounds that anchor the city's spiritual geography; the first sits directly on the Chao Phraya River, the second holds the reclining Buddha and a traditional Thai massage school. A canal cruise threads through historic waterways where residential life continues alongside the surrounding city. A tuk-tuk returns you toward the hotel district. The remainder of the day is unscheduled: wander the Khao San Road area, move through markets, or sample street food stalls that line the sois around your hotel.

atom: Mae Sai border market — browse Burmese goods and cross-border street commerce

Departure from Koh Samui
After breakfast, you have free time until checkout before meeting your representative for transfer to Samui airport and your flight onward.

atom: Ngo Dong River — take a rowing boat trip passing through three water tunnels

Ninh Binh Exploration: Tam Coc and Mua Cave
A rowing boat trip up the Ngo Dong River lasts about 90 minutes, passing through three water tunnels while viewing rice fields and local farmers working and fishing. The landscape of high green mountains creates a distinctive visual effect. Continue to Mua Cave, constructed with nearly 500 stone steps ascending the mountain peak to a viewpoint over the plateau.

atom: Shennv Valley — take an excursion to explore
day_text:
Three Gorges: Qutang, Wu Gorge & Goddess Stream
After breakfast, your guide meets you at the Yangtze deluxe Cruise. The ship sails through the Qutang Gorge and Wu Gorge, two of the Three Gorges of the Yangtze River, renowned for scenery designated the highest level by China's National Tourism Administration. You'll take an excursion to the Shennv Valley, known as the Goddess Stream, where thousands of cliffs hang vertically against the sky. Hundreds-of-meters-high blue peaks create narrow gaps between towering stone walls—a landscape that reveals why this place bears its evocative name. In the evening, join the captain's farewell banquet. You remain accommodated aboard the Yangtze deluxe Cruise.

Departure

Trek from Phu to Nar: Narrow Canyon and Evening Monastery Prayers

atom: Kardung La — drive to and view panoramic vistas

Kardung La Pass and the Nubra Valley Approach

The road climbs 2,000 meters north from Leh, leading toward the Nubra Valley—a region only recently opened to foreign visitors. The ascent rewards with panoramic views across the Indus Valley to the Zanskar Range, where Stok Kangri stands prominently among the higher peaks. At the pass itself, the thin atmosphere frames views of the lesser-known Eastern Karakoram peaks. After pausing for tea at altitude, we return by jeep to Leh, descending back to 3,524 meters and to the hotel for the evening.

Arrival in Kathmandu

Arrival at Delhi & Transfer to Neemrana

day_text:
Nagadeepa Temple & Departure for Trincomalee
Visit Nagadeepa Temple before beginning your journey southward to Trincomalee. Check into your accommodation as evening settles.

Arrival in Colombo
Bandaranaike International Airport staff will meet you on arrival. A driver and English-speaking guide transfer you to your accommodation in the capital, where the rest of the day is yours to rest after travel.

atom: village homestay on the backwaters — stay overnight

Thekkady to Kerala Backwaters: Village Homestay

Phuket Sightseeing: Karon Viewpoint, Big Buddha & Old Town

Thimphu: Yoga at Dochu La & Traditional Medicine

day_text:
Tashigang: Bamboo Forests and Handloom Traditions
A 180-kilometre drive through bamboo forests brings you to Tashigang. Stop at Dewathang, a historical battlefield, then visit Khaling National Handloom, Chorten Kora, and a local home.

day_text:
Jeju: Your Day to Explore
This day is unstructured. Available options include:

- Olle Trail: 437-kilometre loop circumnavigating the island's edge; Routes 6 and 7 are popular sections (flexible half-day or full-day options available)

- Independent exploration of Jeju City

Your CEO can advise on logistics and help arrange transportation to and from trailheads.

atom: Xixiangchi Temple — pass through as first major waypoint on descent
day_text:
Mount Emei: Full-Day Descent Through Temples & Monasteries
A demanding 8 to 9 hour hiking day requires an early start. You descend via cable car to Jieyin Hall, then walk to Leidongping before beginning the descent along old stone steps. Xixiangchi Temple, also known as Elephant Bathing Pool at 2,070 meters, marks the first major waypoint; legend holds that the white elephant of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva once bathed in the pool before the temple. The path continues to Zuantian Slope (Slope Drilling into Sky), a dramatically steep descent of 300 meters with 32 hairpin turns and over 1,500 steps. After resting at Jiuling Hill you hike onward to Yuxian Temple through a section of rolling terrain. Passing Xianfeng Temple, you enter the Ecological Monkey Zone, home to a large wild monkey population. From Wuxiangang parking lot, an eco-bus returns you to the tourist center and your guesthouse.

atom: Tangalle — stay four nights with optional water sports and Ayurvedic spa treatments
day_text:
Arrival and Transfer to The Walawwa, Kotugoda
Airport assistance and welcome on arrival. Transfer to The Walawwa, an 18th-century manor house set within century-old tropical gardens in Kotugoda. Check in and settle for the first night in one of the property's restored rooms.

atom: Nikko — arrange dinner independently at a restaurant in town
day_text:
Shiobara to Nikko: The Cedar Avenue & Sacred Samurai Road — 70 kilometers
Depart Shiobara and cycle through a short walk in Ryu-o-kyo Gorge, then continue via scenic countryside roads and historical sites southward. atom: Gokyo Lake (Dudh Pokhari) — view emerald waters reflecting Cho Oyu and Gyachung Kang

A steady 4–5 hour climb along the valley's side as rhododendron forest transitions to scrub juniper with increasing altitude. The trail passes seasonal herding settlements, used when yaks are brought to these high pastures to graze during summer months. Excellent forward views of Cho Oyu dominate the landscape; behind, the peaks of Kantega and Thamserku frame the valley. We arrive at Machhermo—situated at 4,410 meters—in time for lunch. The day ends at a lodge in Machhermo with full board accommodation.

atom: Cheonjiyeon Waterfall — visit the three-tiered cascade
day_text:
Jeongbang Waterfall, Jeju Olle Trail & Seongsan Ilchulbong
Begin at Jeongbang Waterfall, the only waterfall in Asia that flows directly into the ocean. Trek a section of the Jeju Olle Trail, a network of coastal and countryside footpaths that circle Jeju Island. Continue to Seongsan Ilchulbong, also known as Sunrise Peak, a UNESCO World Heritage Site formed by hydrovolcanic eruptions over 5,000 years ago. The hike to the summit takes roughly an hour and rewards with panoramic views across the island and the surrounding sea. The rest of the day is free. Options include Jungmun Beach; Cheonjiyeon Waterfall, a three-tiered cascade in a forested valley; the Seogwipo Maritime Park with coastal walking paths; Saeyeongyo Bridge, a cable-stayed span over a deep ravine; or sunset drinks at The Cliff, a waterfront bar. Your guide provides information on all options.

atom: Marine Drive — walk the seafront

Mumbai: Elephanta Caves and Colonial Districts

Return to the city for a guided walk through key landmarks: Dhobi Ghat's open-air laundry, the seafront sweep of Marine Drive, Crawford Market's crowded stalls, and the late-19th-century mansions dotting the Colaba neighborhood.

atom: Udawalawe National Park — go on a sunrise jeep safari to observe herds of wild elephants and crocodile populations

Phakding to Namche Bazaar Through Sagarmatha National Park
The trek involves repeated crossings of the Dudh Kosi on high-suspension bridges. Beyond Monjo lies the entrance to Sagarmatha National Park, established to protect the fragile mountain environment. As the trail ascends toward Namche (3,440m), Mount Everest appears in the distance, weather permitting. Namche serves as the main trading hub of the Khumbu, hosting a Saturday market where Hindu traders from the lowlands meet Tibetan yak caravans that have crossed the glaciated Nangpa La. Tea Estate Trails & Ella Rock

atom: Kouri Island — visit coastal viewpoint

Okinawa's Wartime Heritage and Royal Legacy
A guided bus tour examines Okinawa's cultural history and World War II legacy. You then visit the Former Japanese Navy Underground Headquarters, a subterranean complex that provides historical context on the peninsula's wartime role. The Himeyuri Peace Museum follows—a deeply considered memorial to the young women who served as nurses during the final campaign of the Pacific War. At Peace Memorial Park, time is set aside for reflection and remembrance. The tour concludes at Road Station ITOMAN, where local artisans and food producers sell traditional crafts and Okinawan preserves, a practical point for gathering regional provisions.

Tea Estate Trails & Ella Rock
After breakfast, walk through tea estates above Bandarawela and Haputale. The Ella Rock Trail offers moderate ridge walking with views across the plateau. Overnight at The Hideaway.

Old Tingri to Saga

day_text:
Departure from Nepal
Our airport representative will assist with your checkout procedure and escort you to the airport for your final departure from Nepal and onward journey.

atom: Akha hill-tribe village — visit village and taste green tea at plantation
day_text:
Bangkok's Grand Temples and Royal Palace
Begin your Bangkok exploration at Wat Traimit, the Temple of the Golden Buddha, where a 3-meter-high solid gold Buddha carved in Sukhothai style commands the sanctuary. This sculpture weighs 5.5 tons and represents one of Thailand's most significant religious artworks.

Continue to Wat Pho, Bangkok's oldest and largest temple, which houses the largest Reclining Buddha in Thailand. Wat Pho also held historical significance as Thailand's first public education center, reflecting its role in Thai cultural and religious life.

The afternoon brings you to the Grand Palace, built by King Rama I in 1782 as the former residence of Thai monarchs. This sprawling complex remains the most prominent and important site in Bangkok. Within its walls lies Wat Phra Kaew, the Temple of the Emerald Buddha, home to a 48-centimeter jade Buddha sculpture carved in 15th-century southern China from a single piece of emerald-colored jade. The sculpture wears three ceremonial garments that are changed at different times throughout the year.

The palace grounds showcase nine towers and a Pantheon of the Kings, distinguished by golden domes, inspired capitals, decorative murals, and ceramic details. Interior rooms of note include the Throne Room, Official Reception Hall, and Coronation Hall, though the latter closes on Saturdays, Sundays, public holidays, and special occasions.

Breakfast is served at your hotel before departure. The afternoon is left at leisure to rest or explore at your own pace before returning to your Bangkok hotel for the night.

atom: Mon La — cross Mon La before descending to Phortse Tenga

Delhi Departure

atom: Ella Rock Trail — walk a moderate ridge with views across the plateau

Arrival in Seoul: Cheonggyecheon Stream and Myeongdong Orientation
Arrive in Seoul throughout the day and check into Hotel Prince (or similar). As fellow travellers settle in at their own pace, there are no planned activities until the evening group meeting.

At 6 p.m., meet your CEO and fellow travellers for your Welcome Moment. This is your opportunity to connect with your group and learn what to expect from the tour ahead. Your CEO will brief you on the practicalities of travelling through South Korea—where to find supermarkets, main squares, ATMs, and other essentials—before heading out on an orientation walk.

The walk begins at Cheonggyecheon Stream, an 8.4-kilometre waterway restored as a public space that cuts through the heart of downtown Seoul. The walk covers approximately 2 kilometres and takes 45–60 minutes at a leisurely pace. As you walk, you'll pass small waterfalls and nearly two dozen overhead bridges, gaining a sense of the city's geography and character. This restored stream is both a functional transport corridor and a gathering place for locals, offering a calm counterpoint to Seoul's intensity.

From there, you'll move into Myeongdong, a densely packed commercial district situated roughly 20 minutes' walk from the stream. The neighbourhood is a sensory experience—street food carts line the pavements, major shopping malls tower overhead, and entertainment venues draw crowds constantly. It's a quintessential Seoul experience and a good introduction to the city's commercial heart.

After the orientation walk, you have the option to join your CEO and fellow travellers for a group dinner, or explore on your own. Check the notice board in your hotel lobby (or ask reception) for the official meeting time and place if you'd like to join the group.

Before you venture out, it's worth noting that South Korea's efficient train network will be your main transport method throughout this tour. You'll spend most days on foot and will need to carry your own luggage through busy train stations and crowded streets. Please ensure you are fit enough to manage this level of daily movement and comfortable carrying your belongings for extended periods.

The complex is recognized by UNESCO as the most extensive collection of preserved ancient wooden structures in the world. After walking through the palace grounds, you move through the hutongs—traditional alleyways formed by lines of courtyard dwellings—where the daily rhythm of Old Beijing is visible. The day concludes with a metro ride to the Temple of Heaven before returning by subway to your hotel. Wear comfortable shoes for extensive walking.

The 70-kilometre route gradually changes from flat terrain to rolling hills as it approaches the Thai border. The destination is Preah Vihear, a Hindu temple complex from the Angkorian period, built atop the Poy Tady Cliff in the Dangrek Mountains at 525 metres elevation. The site is UNESCO-protected and renowned not only for its architecture but for its dramatic clifftop position with panoramic views of the surrounding landscape and into Thailand. A 4-wheel-drive vehicle ascends to the temple top for two hours of exploration. Most visitors are Khmer pilgrims who have travelled considerable distances to view the handiwork of their ancestors. day_text:
Busan's Markets and Coastal Villages; Return to Seoul by Train
This full day bridges two cities, beginning in Busan's vibrant commercial and cultural quarters before an afternoon train journey to Seoul, where evening exploration awaits.

Start your morning at Jagalchi Fish Market, Busan's major attraction situated at Nampo Port. The market sprawls across countless stalls brimming with fresh seafood, covering approximately 1 hectare with multiple levels. Allow 1–1.5 hours to explore. Watch as locals engage in spirited haggling and fishmongers hawk their catch—the market remains a sensory immersion into the rhythms of a working fishing port.

Next, head to Gukje Market, positioned near BIFF Square, roughly 10 minutes' walk away, Busan's well-known modern movie district. This market carries historical weight: it emerged as a refuge for those seeking livelihood during the Korean War and has evolved into a bustling international marketplace. Today it stocks food, home goods, clothes, souvenirs, and more across its crowded lanes—a living record of Busan's postwar transformation.

Continue to Yongdusan Park, approximately 1.5 kilometres away, a green space home to more than 70 different tree species. The park's distinctive shape is said to resemble a dragon's head. Here stands the 118-meter-high Busan Tower, offering a vantage point across the city and coast. The park provides both natural respite and architectural landmark in one visit.

Before departing Busan, explore Gamcheon Culture Village, situated uphill on a mountainside roughly 20 minutes' drive from the waterfront. The village features uniquely painted houses, vibrant murals, small cafes, and independent shops—a testament to grassroots urban creativity. Its narrow lanes and artistic atmosphere have made it one of Busan's most photographed quarters. Plan for 1.5–2 hours of walking through the village.

Board the high-speed train for your 2.5-hour journey to Seoul. The bullet train departs Busan Station and arrives at Seoul Central Station, departing mid-afternoon to allow evening exploration in Seoul. Transfers are by private vehicle or taxi from the station.

Upon arrival in Seoul, visit Namdaemun Market, Korea's oldest traditional market, established in 1414. It remains the largest, with over 10,000 vendors distributed across several city blocks covering approximately 1.7 hectares. The scale and variety can overwhelm—prepare to navigate crowded aisles stocked with goods ranging from clothing and cosmetics to food and housewares. Allow 1–2 hours to move through the market. The market represents Seoul's commercial DNA and remains a vital gathering point.

Take the cable car up Mount Namsan to reach N Seoul Tower, perched 480 metres above sea level. The cable car journey takes approximately 5–7 minutes and covers 750 metres. Originally built as a broadcasting station, it has evolved into Seoul's most iconic public landmark. The tower's clean lines and prominent hilltop position have made it a fixture in Korean film and television. The cable car journey itself offers views across the city as you ascend.

Entry to the base of N Seoul Tower is included; however, ascending to the observation deck requires an additional fee of 16,000 KRW per person. The observatory provides 360-degree panoramic views of Seoul, encompassing the surrounding neighbourhoods, the Han River, and distant mountains on clear days. Many visitors find the vantage point essential to understanding Seoul's scale and layout.

Your evening remains open for optional activities. The Banpo Bridge Rainbow Fountain, accessible by metro or taxi approximately 10 minutes from N Seoul Tower, offers free viewing and operates throughout the day and evening. The fountain is the world's longest bridge fountain, fitted with nearly 10,000 LED lights and 380 water-spraying nozzles synchronized to music. During daylight, the fountain displays varied configurations evoking willow branches. After sunset, LED illumination transforms it into a dancing rainbow spectacle—a technical achievement that has become a must-see for many visitors.

Alternatively, spend your evening in the Gangnam district, historically rich and fast-developing. Gangnam Station, the busiest subway hub in Seoul, houses a sprawling underground shopping centre roughly 20 minutes from the tower. The district offers the option to visit Bongeunsa, a Buddhist temple situated centrally in Gangnam, or to experience the neighbourhood's restaurants and nightlife venues.

A third option: visit the floating islands, a culture complex comprising three man-made islands near one end of the Banpo Bridge, approximately 10 minutes from N Seoul Tower by taxi or metro. LED lighting creates atmospheric night views, positioning them as a complementary evening destination to the bridge fountain nearby.

Breakfast is included today. You will stay at Hotel Prince or a similar property.
